Anya: Bringing up phoenix-34b (open-source variant) in int4 on the dedicated pool — after ~2h of steady traffic some sessions hit hard OOMs. Any ideas if int4 makes KV/prefix caching fragment faster?

Jia: Can you paste the exact error and the serving config? Also what's current max_new_tokens and batch settings?

Anya: Logs snapshot below. Running on dedicated-gpu-8 with prefix caching enabled. max_new_tokens=1024, max_batch_tokens=8192.

```
[2026-01-15T12:34:22Z] ERROR serve: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-01-15T12:34:22Z] WARN serve: fragmentation_ratio=0.87, total_alloc=64.3GB, free_contiguous=1.2GB
[2026-01-15T12:34:22Z] INFO kvcache: active_prefixes=4321, avg_prefix_len=1200
[2026-01-15T12:34:23Z] ERROR model: allocation failed during new_kv_append, falling back -> session abort
```

Omar: Oof. fragmentation 0.87 is pretty high. Two quick checks: 1) run memtracker to see allocation pattern, 2) are we leaking small allocations from quant routines?

Omar: Run `rwinf memtrack --allocs --since 5m --group-by=callsite` and paste output.

Anya: memtrack output (trimmed):

```
top alloc callers:
  42%  nv_malloc_chunk (0x7ff...)
  23%  kvcache_append
  11%  quant_dequant_buffer
  8%   attention_kv_store
  others 16%
```

Anya: Looks like kvcache_append + small quant buffers are the hot ones. Also saw higher tail-latency on big prompts in canary evals.

Priya: We saw similar with phi2 int8 -> int4 experiments: quant_dequant spikes create lots of transient small allocations that fragment the pool. Two options: drop to int8 for now or change allocator / use pooling to reuse small quant buffers.

Jia: Short-term mitigation: reduce max_new_tokens and batch token window, enable more aggressive kv pruning. Suggested temporary config: 

```
{
  "max_new_tokens": 512,
  "max_batch_tokens": 2048,
  "kv_prune_interval_ms": 60000,
  "kv_prune_threshold": 0.6,
  "prefix_caching": true
}
```

Jia: Also try `--quant-buffer-pool=enabled` flag in runtime to reuse small buffers.

Omar: For quality we should validate: int4 showed a small regression on the intent classification eval set (~1.8% lower exact match). Priya, can you run the 10k eval suite on int8 vs int4?

Priya: On it. I'll start a 10k run against the eval harness (sha: 3f2a1ef). If int4 regression > 1% we should canary int8 and continue allocator work.

buildbot: deploybot: Created rollout: canary -> phoenix-34b-int8 dplat-1 (10% traffic) by Anya. Monitor window 30m. Logs forwarded to #eng-ml-monitoring. :rocket:

Anya: Canary started with the changes (max_new_tokens=512, max_batch_tokens=2048) and int8 for the canary. Also disabled prefix caching for canary to see effect: `prefix_caching=false`. Will report if OOMs reappear.

Jia: Good. After 30m check for: OOMs, fragmentation ratio, avg tail latency, output-quality diffs. If no OOMs and quality is stable, we can plan a staged rollout and simultaneously land buffer-pool patch.

Omar: Also file a follow-up ticket for runtime allocator improvement: reduce small-allocation churn from quant routines + add lifecycle hooks to recycle quant buffers. I can draft the patch.

Priya: Eval halfway: int4 vs int8 shows 1.9% EM drop on the current vetted set. Recommending keep int8 until buffer-pool lands.

Anya: Thanks — will keep canary running for 2h and ramp if clean. Will push patch for config defaults: set default max_new_tokens to 512 for phoenix-34b on dedicated pools until we finish allocator improvements. :thumbsup:

Jia: Thanks all. If anyone sees OOMs or strange errors ping @infra-oncall and drop logs in #incidents.
